noncomputable section

/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter package.  Its scalar carrier
uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
is `def:admissible` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
structure AdmissibleParams where
  q : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  d : ℕ
  hd : 1 ≤ d
  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
  hdvd : m ∣ q

/-- The positivity of the ambient dimension is a proof obligation implicit in
the admissibility convention `def:admissible`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
theorem AdmissibleParams.one_le_m (P : AdmissibleParams) : 1 ≤ P.m := by
  sorry

/-- The fixed model accessor for an admissible parameter package.  It is a
compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently
quantified field representation.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`; paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
noncomputable def AdmissibleParams.model (P : AdmissibleParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq

/-- The low-degree parameter view of an admissible Pauli-test package.  This is
a Lean-only bridge supporting the statement closure; it is not an additional
hypothesis of `thm:pauli`.  Blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
def AdmissibleParams.toLdParams (P : AdmissibleParams) : LdParams where
  q := P.q
  m := P.m
  d := P.d
  k := 1
  hm := P.one_le_m
  hd := P.hd
  hk := by decide
  hq := P.hq
  hdvd := P.hdvd

/-- The scalar carrier associated with an admissible parameter package.  It is
the globally fixed field carrier selected by `AdmissibleParams.model` in
`def:admissible`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
abbrev PauliScalar (P : AdmissibleParams) := P.model.K

/-- The six families of Pauli-test questions.  This is part of
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
inductive PauliType where
  | point (W : PauliKind)
  | aline (W : PauliKind)
  | dline (W : PauliKind)
  | pauli (W : PauliKind)
  | pairW (W : PauliKind)
  | pair
  | ms (t : MsType)
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype

   942	\begin{equation*}
   943	\gamma = \tr \bigl( (\ind_{m}(u_\xpt) \cdot r_\xpt) \cdot
   944	      (\ind_{m}(u_\zpt) \cdot r_\zpt) \bigr)\;.
   945	\end{equation*}
   946	If $\gamma = 0$, then these two measurements commute, and if $\gamma = 1$, then these two measurements anticommute
   947	(this fact is established in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness} below).
   948	In the $\gamma = 0$ case, the verifier can check whether these two measurements commute by performing the ``commutation check'',
   949	which asks the provers to simultaneously measure both $\tr(g_{h_X}(u_X) \cdot r_X)$ and $\tr(g_{h_Z}(u_Z) \cdot r_Z)$ and report their values.
   950	In the $\gamma = 1$ case, on the other hand, the measurements anticommute, which implies that they cannot simultaneously be measured.
   951	In spite of this, the verifier can still check that the measurements anticommute by using the Magic Square game from Section~\ref{sec:ms} above.
   952	As was shown in Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}, any pair of anticommuting measurements
   953	can be used to form a perfect strategy for the Magic Square game
   954	(and indeed the reverse is true as well: any perfect strategy for the Magic Square game entails a pair of anticommuting measurements).
   955	
   956	Together, these give the main subtests for the game $\game^\pauli$.

   965	We now describe the question distribution of the game $\game^\pauli$, and show

  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on
  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where
  1117	$(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice,\tvar_\bob,x_\bob)$ is sampled by first uniformly
  1118	sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice,\tvar_\bob)$ from the graph $G^\pauli$ defined
  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.

   195	      match W with
   196	      | .X => u (.inl (.inl j))

   198	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) =>
   199	      match W with
   200	      | .X => 0
   201	      | .Z => u (.inl (.inl j))
   202	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => u (.inl (.inr ()))
   203	  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)
   204	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   205	  | .inr _ => 0

   211	def pauliSharedProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliSpace P :=
   212	  fun i => match i with
   213	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))))
   214	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))))
   215	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => 0
   216	  | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
   217	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   218	  | .inr _ => z (.inr ())

   229	  | .aline _ => 2
   230	  | .dline _ => 3
   231	  | .pauli _ => 0

   241	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.

   250	  | .pairW _ => pauliSharedProjection
   251	  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/

    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]

    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one

    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/

   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl

   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl

   803	\section{Expanding the Hilbert space and defining commuting observables}
   804	\label{sec:expanding}
   805	
   806	The next step of the analysis adjoins ancillary EPR registers to the
   807	players' state and lifts the strategy observables and measurements to the
   808	expanded state. The point of the construction is that the ancilla factor of
   809	each lifted observable carries the \emph{exact} Pauli commutation sign, so
   810	that the signs cancel and the lifted observables approximately commute for

    51	\begin{definition}
    52	Given integer $d,m$ and a prime power $q$ we denote by $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ the set of polynomials in $m$ variables
    53	  with \emph{individual} degree at most $d$ in each variable. When the field is clear from context we write $\ideg_{d,m}$. 	
    54		When
    55	  the number of variables is clear from context we
    56	  write $\ideg_d$. We denote by $\deg_{d}$ the set of polynomials with
    57	  \emph{total} degree at most $d$.
    58	\end{definition}
    59	
    60	Recall the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}, in which vectors $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ get mapped to polynomials $g_h \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ such that for every $u \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_h(u) = h_u$ where the coordinates of $h$ are indexed by binary strings of length $m$. For $x\in \F_q^m$, recall the definition of the vector $\ind_m(x) \in \F_q^\nqubits$ from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}. Recall also the finite field trace $\tr(\cdot)=\tr_{q\to 2}(\cdot):\F_q\to\F_2$, where $q=2^k$ for odd $k$, defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. 
    61	
    62	
    63	
    64	Call a tuple $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) \in (\F_q^m)^2
    65	\times (\F_q)^2$ \emph{anticommuting} if the quantity 
    66	 \[\gamma\,=\,\tr ((r_\xpt \cdot
    67	\ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt)))\]
    68	introduced in~\Cref{eq:gamma-value} is not $0$, and \emph{commuting} if $\gamma=0$.
    69	
    70	\begin{fact}
    71	\label{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
    72		The probability that a tuple $\omega= (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ sampled uniformly at random from $(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$
    73		is anti-commuting is at least 
    74		\[
    75			(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big (1 - \frac{md}{q} \Big )  \cdot \frac{1}{2} \geq \Big (1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}.
    76		\]
    77		The probability that $\omega$ is commuting is also at least $\Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.
    78	\end{fact}
    79	\begin{proof}
    80		First, note that $\ind_m(u_\xpt) = 0$ if and only if $u_\xpt = 0$. If $u_\xpt=0$ then $\omega$ is commuting. Otherwise, if $u_\xpt \neq 0$, then observe that for all $r_\xpt, r_\zpt, u_\zpt$,
    81		\begin{align*}
    82			\tr( (r_\xpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot
    83	                \ind_m(u_\zpt))) &= \tr( r_\xpt r_\zpt (\ind_m(u_\xpt) \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt))) \\
    84									&= \tr( (r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt))\;,
    85		\end{align*}
    86		where $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}$ is a nonzero polynomial in $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$.
    87		
    88		If $r_\xpt = 0$, then $\omega$ is commuting. Condition on $r_\xpt \neq 0$.  Since $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}\neq 0$ has total degree at most $md$, by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma the probability that $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is zero over a uniformly random choice of $u_\zpt$ is at most $md/q$. Conditioned on $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$, the product $(r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ when $r_\zpt$ is chosen uniformly at random. 
    89		
    90		The probability that $u_\xpt \neq 0, r_\xpt \neq 0, g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$ is at least $(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot (1 - md/q)$ since $u_\xpt, r_\xpt, u_\zpt$ are chosen independently.
    91		
    92		Since $q = 2^t$ is an admissible field size, we have that for all $a \in \F_q$, the trace of $a$ is equal to $\sum_i a_i$ where $(a_1,\ldots,a_t)=\kappa(a) \in \F_2^t$ are defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. Thus the probability that a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ has trace $0$ is exactly $1/2$. 
    93	\end{proof}

    95	In this appendix we often use the ``$\approx_\delta$'' notation to specify closeness of general operators (not necessarily POVMs) that are indexed by questions but not answers: given sets of operators $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ indexed by questions $x \in \cal{X}$, we write $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote \[
    96		\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x)
    97	        \ket{\psi}\,\leq\, O(\delta)
    98	      \]
    99	where $\mu$ is a question distribution and $\ket{\psi}$ is a state that has been fixed by context. This will be useful for expressing closeness of observables, for example. The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and weighted sums of those operators. 
   100	\begin{lemma}
   101	\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   102	Let $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by some finite set $\mathcal{X}$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$. Let $\{\alpha_x \}$ be a set of complex numbers such that $|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. Then if $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over $x$ drawn from $\mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$, where $A = \E_x \alpha_x A^x$ and $B= \E_x \alpha_x B^x$.
   103	\end{lemma}
   104	\begin{proof}
   105	Expand
   106	\begin{align*}
   107		\Big\| \E_x \alpha_x \big ( A^x - B^x \big) \ket{\psi} \Big\|^2 &\leq \Big( \E_x \norm{ (A^x -B^x) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   108		&\leq \E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   109		&\leq \delta\;.
   110	\end{align*}
   111	The first inequality is the triangle inequality and the second inequality is Jensen's inequality. 
   112	\end{proof}
   113	
   114	\begin{lemma}
   115	\label{lem:povm-to-obs}
   116	Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set. Let $\{A^x_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be POVMs and let $\{ \alpha_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a collection of complex numbers on the unit circle. Let $A^x = \sum_a \alpha_a A^x_a$ and $B^x = \sum_a  \alpha_a B^x_a$. Then 
   117	\[
   118		A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a \quad \text{implies} \quad A^x \approx_{\delta'} B^x
   119	\]
   120	for $\delta' = |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta$.
   121	\end{lemma}
   122	\begin{proof}
   123	Expand
   124		\begin{align*}
   125			\E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \Big\|\sum_a \alpha_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}\Big\|^2 \\
   126			&\leq \E_x \Big( \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   127			&\leq \E_x |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   128			&\leq |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta\;.
   129		\end{align*}
   130	The first inequality follows from the triangle inequality, the second inequality follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, and the last inequality follows from the assumption that $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$. 
   131	\end{proof}

    37	\begin{definition}[Individual and total degree polynomial classes]
    38		\label{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
    39		\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc}
    40		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.TotalDegreePoly}
    41		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.DegPoly, MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient}

    44		\uses{def:line, def:line-representative, def:polyfunc}
    45		Given integers $d, m \geq 0$ and a prime power $q$, denote by
    46		$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ the set of polynomials in $m$ variables over
    47		$\F_q$ with \emph{individual} degree at most $d$ in each variable. When
    48		the field is clear from context we write $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}$, and when
    49		the number of variables is also clear from context, $\mathrm{ideg}_d$. We
    50		denote by $\deg_d$ the set of polynomials with \emph{total} degree at
    51		most $d$.
    52		% The line-restricted classes below are introduced only implicitly in the
    53		% source, in the statement of the lemma labelled lem:qld-comm-line-cons,
    54		% which reads them as polynomials "defined on the line". The coefficient
    55		% reading adopted here follows the answer format of the decision procedure
    56		% of the low individual degree game (source figure fig:ld-decider) and the
    57		% representative convention of def:polyfunc; see the remark following this
    58		% definition.
    59		For a line $\ell \subseteq \F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line}) presented
    60		by a base point $u_0$ and a direction $v$ --- for the lines arising as
    61		question contents, the pair read off the line's description, whose base
    62		point is the canonical representative of
    63		Definition~\ref{def:line-representative} --- and an integer $c \geq 0$,
    64		we write $\deg_c(\ell)$ for the set of univariate polynomials of degree
    65		at most $c$, each given by its list of $c+1$ coefficients and identified
    66		by its polynomial representative rather than by the function it induces,
    67		as in Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}; the argument $\ell$ records the
    68		line to which such an answer refers, through the parameterization
    69		$t \mapsto u_0 + tv$. The cases used below are $\deg_d(\ell)$ and
    70		$\deg_{md}(\ell)$; whenever $d \leq md$, extending coefficient lists by
    71		zeros gives the inclusion $\deg_d(\ell) \subseteq \deg_{md}(\ell)$. For
    72		$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$, $u \in \ell$, and $a \in \F_q$, we say that $f$
    73		\emph{evaluates to $a$ at $u$}, written $f(u) = a$, if $f(t) = a$ for
    74		every $t \in \F_q$ with $u = u_0 + tv$. When $v \neq 0$ this $t$ is
    75		unique, so every $f$ evaluates at every point of $\ell$; when $v = 0$,
    76		so that $\ell = \{u_0\}$, exactly those $f$ that induce a constant
    77		function on $\F_q$ evaluate at $u_0$, to their constant value. An
    78		operator indexed by $f(u)$ is understood to be the zero operator when
    79		$f$ does not evaluate at $u$, and for a family $\{N_f\}$ indexed by
    80		$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$ we write
    81		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]} = \sum_{f \colon f(u) = a} N_f$; when
    82		$v = 0$ the classes indexed by $a \in \F_q$ form a sub-measurement
    83		rather than a partition of the outcomes. The \emph{completed} family of
    84		evaluation classes is the family indexed by $a \in \F_q \cup \{\bot\}$
    85		obtained by adjoining the additional class
    86		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]} = \sum_{f} N_f$, the sum over those
    87		$f$ that do not evaluate at $u$; when $\{N_f\}$ is a POVM,
    88		respectively a projective measurement, the completed classes form one
    89		as well, and when $v \neq 0$ the class
    90		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]}$ is the zero operator.
    91	\end{definition}

   282	\begin{definition}[Closeness of question-indexed operators]
   283		\label{def:approx-question-indexed-operators}
   284		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.opDistSq}
   285		\leanok
   286		\uses{def:povm-distance}
   287		Let $\{A^x\}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be families of operators (not necessarily
   288		POVM elements) indexed by questions $x \in \mathcal{X}$ but not by
   289		answers, let $\mu$ be a distribution over $\mathcal{X}$, and let
   290		$\ket{\psi}$ be a state, both fixed by context. Write
   291		$A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote
   292		\[
   293			\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi} \,\leq\, O(\delta)\,.
   294		\]
   295		This extends the answer-indexed closeness of
   296		Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance} to answer-free families of operators,
   297		such as observables; as there, the right-hand side allows a hidden
   298		universal constant.
   299	\end{definition}
   300	
   301	The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and
   302	weighted sums of those operators.
   303	
   304	\begin{lemma}
   305		\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   306		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.avg_closeness}
   307		\leanok
   308		\uses{def:approx-question-indexed-operators}
   309		Let $\{A^x\}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by a finite set
   310		$\mathcal{X}$, let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over
   311		$\mathcal{X}$, and let $\{\alpha_x\}$ be complex numbers with
   312		$|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. If $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over
   313		$x \sim \mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$ for the single operators
   314		$A = \E_{x} \alpha_x A^x$ and $B = \E_{x} \alpha_x B^x$, regarded as
   315		indexed by a one-element question set; quantitatively,
   316		% The closeness of Definition def:approx-question-indexed-operators
   317		% carries a hidden universal constant on both sides; the quantitative
   318		% sentence records the constant-free inequality the proof establishes.
   319		\[
   320			\big\| (A - B) \ket{\psi} \big\|^2
   321			\,\leq\, \E_x \big\| (A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi} \big\|^2\,,
   322		\]
   323		so the conclusion holds with the same implicit constant as the
   324		hypothesis.
   325	\end{lemma}
   326	\begin{proof}
   327		Expand
   328		\[
   329			\Big\| \E_x \alpha_x (A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi} \Big\|^2
   330			\,\leq\, \Big( \E_x \big\| (A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi} \big\| \Big)^2
   331			\,\leq\, \E_x \big\| (A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi} \big\|^2\,,
   332		\]
   333		using the triangle inequality followed by Jensen's inequality; the
   334		right-hand side is at most $O(\delta)$ by the hypothesis, with the same
   335		implicit constant.
   336	\end{proof}

   338	\begin{lemma}
   339		\label{lem:povm-to-obs}
   340		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.povm_to_obs}
   341		\leanok
   342		\uses{def:approx-question-indexed-operators, def:povm-distance}
   343		Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$
   344		and $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be POVMs, and let
   345		$\{\alpha_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be complex numbers on the unit
   346		circle. Let $A^x = \sum_a \alpha_a A^x_a$ and
   347		$B^x = \sum_a \alpha_a B^x_a$. Then
   348		\[
   349			A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a \quad\text{implies}\quad A^x \approx_{\delta'} B^x
   350		\]
   351		for $\delta' = |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta$, where the hypothesis is the
   352		answer-indexed closeness of Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance} and the
   353		conclusion is the question-indexed closeness of
   354		Definition~\ref{def:approx-question-indexed-operators}.
   355	\end{lemma}
   356	\begin{proof}
   357		\uses{def:povm-distance, def:approx-question-indexed-operators}
   358		% The source ends this display with the exact bound |A| * delta; under the
   359		% O(.) reading of def:povm-distance the hypothesis only supplies O(delta),
   360		% and the constant is retained inside the O(.).
   361		Expand
   362		\[
   363			\E_x \Big\| \sum_a \alpha_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} \Big\|^2
   364			\,\leq\, \E_x \Big( \sum_a \big\| (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} \big\| \Big)^2
   365			\,\leq\, |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \E_x \sum_a \big\| (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} \big\|^2
   366			\,\leq\, O\big( |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta \big)\,,
   367		\]
   368		using the triangle inequality followed by the Cauchy--Schwarz
   369		inequality; the last step is the hypothesis
   370		$A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$, whose bound carries a hidden universal
   371		constant (Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}), and the conclusion
   372		holds with the same implicit constant.
   373	\end{proof}

   737		$W^r(u) = \Id - 2 M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{[\tr(\cdot\,r)=1]}$
   738		transfers this to the observables with error $\eps$. For the
   739		anticommuting case: item~\ref{enu:qld-ms-cons} of
   740		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} together with
   741		Lemma~\ref{lem:povm-to-obs} relates $X^{r_X}(u_X)$ and $Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)$
   742		to the Magic Square observables
   743		$M^{\mathrm{Variable}_j,\omega} = M^{\mathrm{Variable}_j,\omega}_0 - M^{\mathrm{Variable}_j,\omega}_1$
   744		for $j \in \{1,5\}$; for each anticommuting $\omega$, the Magic Square
   745		rigidity theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-rigidity}) applied with
   746		$\eps_\omega = 1 - \Lambda_\omega$ gives
   747		$\Id \ot M^{\mathrm{Variable}_1,\omega} M^{\mathrm{Variable}_5,\omega} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps_\omega}} - \Id \ot M^{\mathrm{Variable}_5,\omega} M^{\mathrm{Variable}_1,\omega}$;
   748		averaging over anticommuting $\omega$ with Jensen's inequality
   749		($\E \eps_\omega^{1/2} \leq (\E \eps_\omega)^{1/2} = O(\eps^{1/2})$,
   750		using item~\ref{enu:qld-ms}) and transferring across the tensor factor
   751		with Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}, applied twice, yields the
   752		anticommutation with error $\sqrt{\eps}$. The two cases combine into
   753		the $(-1)^{\gamma(\omega)}$-signed statement over uniformly random
   754		$\omega$, since the uniform average is bounded by the sum of the two
   755		conditional averages.
   756	\end{proof}
   757	
   758	\begin{remark}[Source corrections]
   759		\label{rem:qld-win-implications-typos}
   760		Two typographical slips in the source are corrected above. In
   761		item~\ref{enu:qld-ms} of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} the
   762		source writes the expectation over $\omega$ subject to the condition
   763		$\tr((r_X \cdot u_X) \cdot (r_Z \cdot u_Z)) \neq 0$, omitting the map
   764		$\mathrm{ind}_m$; the intended condition, consistent with the
   765		surrounding text and with Definition~\ref{def:anticommuting-tuple}, is
   766		$\gamma(\omega) \neq 0$, that is, $\omega$ anticommuting, and this is
   767		the form stated above. In the source proof of
   768		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications-obs}, one display reads
   769		$Z^{r_X}(u_X)\,X^{r_Z}(u_Z)$ where $Z^{r_Z}(u_Z)\,X^{r_X}(u_X)$ is
   770		meant.
   771		% A third slip in the source, the label prefix `len' in place of `lem'
   772		% on the lemma corresponding to lem:qld-win-implications-obs, is
   773		% recorded in the comment at that lemma; no alias label is defined.
   774		In addition, the source proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}
   775		restricts attention to the case $6md \leq q$ and disposes of the
   776		remaining parameters by an appeal to Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}, the
   777		theorem whose proof the lemma is part of; that argument does not
   778		establish the unrestricted statement of the lemma, and for $d = 0$ the
   779		probability bound it invokes is false
   780		(Remark~\ref{rem:omega-anticomm-prob-correction}). The proof given
   781		above instead uses the lower bounds of
   782		Lemma~\ref{fact:omega-anticomm-prob} on the probabilities of the
   783		commuting and anticommuting events, which are universal constants for
   784		every admissible parameter tuple, so no restriction on the parameters
   785		is needed.
   786		Finally, the source states item~\ref{enu:qld-ld} of
   787		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} with answer summation over
   788		$a \in \F_q$ only, implicitly reading the evaluation classes of the
   789		line measurement as a complete measurement. Under the coefficient
   790		reading of Definition~\ref{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
   791		(Remark~\ref{rem:deg-line-representatives}) the classes indexed by
   792		$a \in \F_q$ form only a sub-measurement when the line has zero
   793		direction --- a case the question distribution produces with positive
   794		probability (Remark~\ref{rem:ld-win-zero-direction}) --- while the
   795		relation $\simeq_\eps$ of Definition~\ref{def:consistency} is defined
   796		for POVMs. Item~\ref{enu:qld-ld} therefore completes both families by
   797		an explicit $\bot$ outcome; the same implicit completeness assumption
   798		occurs in the source proof of the statement corresponding to
   799		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-line-cons}, whose proof below invokes the
   800		completed families instead.
   801	\end{remark}
   802	
   803	\section{Expanding the Hilbert space and defining commuting observables}
   804	\label{sec:expanding}
   805	
   806	The next step of the analysis adjoins ancillary EPR registers to the
   807	players' state and lifts the strategy observables and measurements to the
   808	expanded state. The point of the construction is that the ancilla factor of
   809	each lifted observable carries the \emph{exact} Pauli commutation sign, so
   810	that the signs cancel and the lifted observables approximately commute for
   811	every tuple $\omega$.
   812	
   813	\begin{definition}[Expanded state]
   814		\label{def:expanded-state}
   815		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SixReg, MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.psiHat}
   816		\leanok
   817		\uses{lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:EPR}
   818		Recall that $M = 2^m$. Introduce registers $\mathsf{A}', \mathsf{A}'',
   819		\mathsf{B}', \mathsf{B}''$, each with Hilbert space isomorphic to
   820		$(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, and define the state
   821		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-psihat}
   822			\ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}
   823			\,=\, (\ket{\psi})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}}
   824			\ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{A}'\mathsf{A}''}
   825			\ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}_{\mathsf{B}'\mathsf{B}''}\,,

     4	/-!
     5	# Generalized Pauli operators and EPR states
     6	
     7	The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
     8	are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
     9	operator algebra.  The Fourier/orthogonality identities are retained as named
    10	proof obligations for subsequent stages.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
    15	and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    27	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    28	
    29	/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in `def:generalized-pauli`,
    30	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    31	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    32	-/
    33	inductive PauliKind where
    34	  | X
    35	  | Z
    36	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    37	
    38	/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.
    40	
    41	It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
    42	character in their statement types. -/
    43	noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    44	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
    45	
    46	/--
    47	The shift operator `τ^X(a)`.  Blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`,
    48	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`; paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    50	-/
    51	noncomputable def tauShift (a : K) : Op K :=
    52	  fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0
    53	
    54	/--
    55	The phase operator `τ^Z(b)`, with the fixed binary trace in the phase.  It is
    56	the second operator of `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 529-571; paper
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`).
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def tauPhase (b : K) : Op K :=
    60	  fun i j => if i = j then phaseSign (binTrace K (b * j)) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- The single-qudit eigenvector coordinate used in the tensor-product basis;
    63	see `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1126-1161`. -/
    64	private noncomputable def singlePauliVec (W : PauliKind) (e x : K) : ℂ :=
    65	  match W with
    66	  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0
    67	  | .X =>
    68	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * phaseSign (binTrace K (e * x))
    69	
    70	/--
    71	The normalized single/multi-qudit eigenvector for a Pauli basis label.  For an
    72	index type `ι`, the input `e : ι → K` labels the tensor-product basis vector.
    73	This is the vector form of `def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint
    74	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:550-570`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`.
    76	-/
    77	noncomputable def pauliVec {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    78	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) (x : ι → K) : ℂ :=
    79	  ∏ i : ι, singlePauliVec W (e i) (x i)
    80	
    81	/--
    82	The rank-one projector onto `pauliVec W e`.  This is the projective measurement
    83	element `τ^W_e` in `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 562-570; paper
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`).
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    87	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    88	  Matrix.vecMulVec (pauliVec W e) (fun x => star (pauliVec W e x))
    89	
    90	/-- A compact operator-valued form of a generalized Pauli observable from
    91	`def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    93	-/
    94	noncomputable def tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    95	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    96	  fun x y =>
    97	    ∏ i : ι,
    98	      match W with
    99	      | .X => tauShift (a i) (x i) (y i)
   100	      | .Z => tauPhase (a i) (x i) (y i)
   101	
   102	/--
   103	The EPR vector on a finite label space.  Blueprint `def:EPR`,
   104	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper origin
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
   106	-/
   107	noncomputable def eprState (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   108	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (V × V) :=
   109	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (V × V) ℂ).symm
   110	    (fun p : V × V =>
   111	      if p.1 = p.2 then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0)
   112	
   113	/-- The EPR vector is normalized on a nonempty finite carrier; see
   114	`def:EPR`, `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`. -/
   115	theorem eprState_norm (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   116	    ‖eprState V‖ = 1 := by
   117	  sorry
   118	
   119	/--
   120	Fourier expansion of a generalized Pauli observable in the Pauli projectors.
   121	This is `lem:pauli-observable-expansion`, equations `eq:pauli-obs-proj` and
   122	`eq:pauli-inversion-0`, in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:638-652`;
   123	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1141-1161`.
   124	Both directions are deliberately left as proof-level obligations in stage 4.1.
   125	-/
   126	theorem tauObservable_eq_sum_pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   127	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) :
   128	    tauObservable W a =
   129	      ∑ e : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • pauliProj W e := by
   130	  sorry
   131	
   132	/-- The inverse Fourier expansion of a Pauli projector
   133	(`lem:pauli-observable-expansion`), blueprint
   134	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:638-652`, paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1141-1161`.
   136	-/
   137	theorem pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   138	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) :
   139	    pauliProj W e =
   140	      (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   141	        ∑ a : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • tauObservable W a := by
   142	  sorry
   143	
   144	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

Restore the sharper standalone theorem. The common `deltaLine` existential wrapper may remain as a separately derived, coarser result.
